RAII C++ wrapper around a spv_context. Manages creation and destruction tied to object lifetime, provides access to the underlying C context and allows setting a message consumer. Constructed with a target environment. Non-copyable, movable.

RAII wrapper for spv_validator_options configuring SPIR-V validation behavior (limits, layout relaxations, friendly names, etc.). Implicitly converts to the underlying C handle. Owns and destroys the options.

RAII wrapper for spv_optimizer_options controlling optimizer behavior (whether to run validator, max id bound, and preservation policies). Implicit conversion to C handle. Owns lifetime of the options.

RAII wrapper for spv_reducer_options configuring reducer behavior (step limit, whether to stop on validation error, target function). Implicitly convertible to the underlying C handle and owns its lifetime.

RAII wrapper for spv_fuzzer_options controlling fuzzer configuration (replay validation, random seed, replay range, shrinker steps, pass validation, enabling all passes). Implicit conversion to the C handle; owns lifetime.

High-level C++ interface to SPIRV-Tools providing assembly, disassembly, parsing, and validation services for a target environment. Maintains an opaque pimpl to manage internal state. Not copyable or movable.

Primary C++ interface for registering and running SPIR-V optimization passes. It owns internal context and pass manager state and provides many helper registration methods and Run overloads. Instances are non-copyable and non-movable; usage is by constructing with a target environment, registering passes, configuring options, and calling Run.

A move-only token that encapsulates a single optimization pass instance or configuration. Tokens are produced by Create*Pass() free functions and consumed by Optimizer::RegisterPass. Internals are hidden behind an opaque Impl pointer.

Options class controlling SPIR-V module linking in spvtools. Encapsulates flags for producing a library vs executable, verifying IDs, allowing partial linkage or pointer type mismatches, selecting highest version, function/variable target and architecture CSV strings, capability toggles, and a list of input file paths. All fields default to disabled/empty values. Construct with default constructor and configure via setters before passing to Link().

functions.name: spvOperandIsConcrete
functions.description: Returns true if the given operand type is concrete (i.e., not optional/variable helper types). Intended for checking operand type categories when parsing/assembling SPIR-V.
requirements: Argument type must be a valid spv_operand_type_t value.

functions.name: spvOperandIsConcreteMask
functions.description: Returns true if the given operand type is both concrete and represents a bitmask kind of operand.
requirements: Argument type must be a valid spv_operand_type_t value.

functions.name: spvSoftwareVersionString
functions.description: Returns a process-lifetime, null-terminated string representing the SPIRV-Tools software version.
requirements: Returned pointer remains valid for the lifetime of the process and must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: spvSoftwareVersionDetailsString
functions.description: Returns a process-lifetime, null-terminated string with project name, version, and commit details.
requirements: Returned pointer remains valid for the lifetime of the process and must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: spvTargetEnvDescription
functions.description: Returns a null-terminated string describing the given SPIR-V target environment enum value.
requirements: env should be a valid spv_target_env value.
Returned pointer must not be freed by the caller (lifetime unspecified but typically static).

functions.name: spvParseTargetEnv
functions.signature: bool spvParseTargetEnv(const char* s, spv_target_env* env);
functions.description: Parses a textual target environment into a spv_target_env. On failure returns false and sets *env to SPV_ENV_UNIVERSAL_1_0.
requirements: s must be a null-terminated C string.
env must be a non-null pointer to receive the parsed value.

functions.name: spvParseVulkanEnv
functions.signature: bool spvParseVulkanEnv(uint32_t vulkan_ver, uint32_t spirv_ver, spv_target_env* env);
functions.description: Determines the least-featured target environment that supports the given Vulkan and SPIR-V versions and writes it to env. Returns true if such a target is supported.
requirements: env must be a non-null pointer.
vulkan_ver must be encoded per Vulkan 29.2.1 (major in bits 22–31, minor in bits 12–21).
spirv_ver must be encoded per the SPIR-V header version word (major in bits 16–23, minor in bits 8–15).

functions.name: spvContextCreate
functions.description: Creates a SPIRV-Tools context object for the given target environment, used across many API calls. Returns NULL if env is invalid.
requirements: env should be a valid spv_target_env value.
Returned context must be destroyed with spvContextDestroy when no longer needed.

functions.name: spvContextDestroy
functions.description: Destroys a context created by spvContextCreate.
requirements: context must be a context previously returned by spvContextCreate; passing NULL is allowed by typical C conventions but not explicitly stated.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsCreate
functions.description: Allocates and returns a validator options object initialized to defaults.
requirements: Returned options object remains valid until destroyed with spvValidatorOptionsDestroy.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsDestroy
functions.description: Destroys a validator options object created by spvValidatorOptionsCreate.
requirements: options must be an object previously returned by spvValidatorOptionsCreate.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetUniversalLimit
functions.signature: void spvValidatorOptionsSetUniversalLimit(spv_validator_options options, spv_validator_limit limit_type, uint32_t limit);
functions.description: Sets the maximum Universal Limit for the given limit type in the validator options.
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.
limit_type must be a valid spv_validator_limit value.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetRelaxStoreStruct
functions.description: Enables/disables relaxing type rules on stores to structs with identical layouts.
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetRelaxLogicalPointer
functions.description: Enables/disables relaxed pointer usage rules in logical addressing mode (e.g., pointer-typed OpVariable, returning pointers).
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetBeforeHlslLegalization
functions.description: Enables/disables relaxation expecting later HLSL legalization optimizations (includes relaxed logical pointers and other pointer argument relaxations; GLSLstd450 Interpolate* first arg relaxed).
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetRelaxBlockLayout
functions.description: Enables/disables relaxed block layout rules (VK_KHR_relaxed_block_layout). Enabled by default for Vulkan 1.1+ targets.
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetUniformBufferStandardLayout
functions.description: Enables/disables use of standard block layout rules for uniform buffers.
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetScalarBlockLayout
functions.description: Enables/disables scalar block layout rules as per VK_EXT_scalar_block_layout.
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetWorkgroupScalarBlockLayout
functions.description: Enables/disables scalar block layout rules for Workgroup blocks (VK_KHR_workgroup_memory_explicit_layout).
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetSkipBlockLayout
functions.description: Enables/disables skipping validation of standard uniform/storage block layout.
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetAllowLocalSizeId
functions.description: Allows or disallows the LocalSizeId decoration where otherwise prohibited by the environment.
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetAllowOffsetTextureOperand
functions.description: Allows Offset (in addition to ConstOffset) for texture operations (VK_KHR_maintenance8).
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetAllowVulkan32BitBitwise
functions.description: Allows base operands of certain bit operations to be non-32-bit wide (VK_KHR_maintenance9).
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvValidatorOptionsSetFriendlyNames
functions.description: Enables/disables using friendly names in validation error messages.
requirements: options must be a valid validator options object.

functions.name: spvOptimizerOptionsCreate
functions.description: Allocates and returns an optimizer options object initialized to defaults.
requirements: Returned options object remains valid until destroyed with spvOptimizerOptionsDestroy.

functions.name: spvOptimizerOptionsDestroy

functions.name: spvOptimizerOptionsSetRunValidator

functions.name: spvOptimizerOptionsSetValidatorOptions

requirements: options must be a valid optimizer options object.

functions.name: spvOptimizerOptionsSetMaxIdBound
functions.description: Sets the maximum possible value for the id bound to be assumed/used by optimizer.

functions.name: spvOptimizerOptionsSetPreserveBindings
functions.description: Configures whether all bindings within the module should be preserved by optimization passes.

functions.name: spvOptimizerOptionsSetPreserveSpecConstants
functions.description: Configures whether all specialization constants within the module should be preserved by optimization passes.

functions.name: spvReducerOptionsCreate

functions.name: spvReducerOptionsDestroy

functions.name: spvReducerOptionsSetStepLimit
functions.description: Sets the maximum number of reduction steps the reducer should perform before giving up.
requirements: options must be a valid reducer options object.

functions.name: spvReducerOptionsSetFailOnValidationError
functions.description: Sets whether the reducer fails on validation error (treat invalid states as terminal) or treats them as uninteresting and backtracks.
requirements: options must be a valid reducer options object.

functions.name: spvReducerOptionsSetTargetFunction
functions.description: Restricts reduction to a specific function result id. If set to 0, the reducer targets all functions and module-level parts. Non-zero id is required to exist.
requirements: options must be a valid reducer options object.
If target_function is non-zero, it must be the result id of an existing function in the module being reduced.

functions.name: spvFuzzerOptionsSetRandomSeed

functions.name: spvFuzzerOptionsSetReplayRange

functions.description: Registers passes described by a list of flags. Emits an error via the message consumer on invalid entries. Returns true on success.
requirements: Each flag string must have a valid form accepted by FlagHasValidForm.
A message consumer should be set to capture error messages if validation fails.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::RegisterPassesFromFlags
functions.description: Registers passes from flags with optional interface preservation. Returns true if all passes are registered successfully.
requirements: Flags must be of a valid form. Invalid flags cause false return and an error message via the consumer.
If preserve_interface is true, non-IO interface variables are preserved.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::RegisterPassFromFlag
functions.description: Registers a single pass based on a flag of the form "--pass_name[=pass_args]", or special flags -O, -Os, or --legalize-hlsl. Returns true if the pass is known and registered.
requirements: flag must be one of: --pass_name[=pass_args], -O, -Os, or --legalize-hlsl.
Unknown flags yield false; a message may be emitted to the consumer.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::RegisterPassFromFlag
functions.description: Registers a single pass from a flag with optional interface preservation. Supports -O, -Os, --legalize-hlsl, and explicit --pass_name[=pass_args].
requirements: flag must have a valid accepted form.
If preserve_interface is true, non-IO interface variables are preserved.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::FlagHasValidForm
functions.description: Checks whether a flag string has a valid form: "--pass_name[=pass_args]", "-O", or "-Os".
requirements: flag must be a non-empty string.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::SetTargetEnv
functions.description: Changes the target environment after creation. Should be called before Run().
requirements: env must be a valid spv_target_env.
Call before any Run() to affect validation/optimization behavior.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::Run
functions.signature: bool spvtools::Optimizer::Run(const uint32_t* original_binary, size_t original_binary_size, std::vector<uint32_t>* optimized_binary) const
functions.description: Optimizes a SPIR-V module and writes the result to optimized_binary. Uses the same SPIR-V version as the input. Validates before transforms and optionally after each, based on options.
requirements: original_binary must point to a buffer of original_binary_size 32-bit words.
optimized_binary must be a valid non-null pointer to a vector to receive results.
original_binary_size is the number of 32-bit words, not bytes.
It is allowed to alias original_binary to the start of optimized_binary's storage.
Returns false if validation fails or a pass reports an error; optimized_binary contents may be invalid on failure.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::Run
functions.signature: bool spvtools::Optimizer::Run(const uint32_t* original_binary, const size_t original_binary_size, std::vector<uint32_t>* optimized_binary, const ValidatorOptions& options, bool skip_validation) const
functions.description: Deprecated Run overload. Optimizes with explicit validator options, optionally skipping validation if the caller guarantees validity.
requirements: original_binary must point to a buffer of original_binary_size 32-bit words.
optimized_binary must be a valid non-null pointer.
If skip_validation is true, the caller guarantees the input module is valid; no validation will run.
options controls validator behavior when validation is performed.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::Run
functions.signature: bool spvtools::Optimizer::Run(const uint32_t* original_binary, const size_t original_binary_size, std::vector<uint32_t>* optimized_binary, const spv_optimizer_options opt_options) const
functions.description: Optimizes with an optimizer-options object controlling validation-before/after and client API validation, among others.
requirements: original_binary must point to original_binary_size 32-bit words.
optimized_binary must be a valid non-null pointer.
opt_options must be a valid spv_optimizer_options object configured as desired.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::GetPassNames
functions.description: Returns the names of all passes added to the optimizer's pass manager. Strings remain valid until the pass manager is destroyed.
requirements: Use returned pointers only while the optimizer (and its pass manager) remain alive.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::SetPrintAll
functions.description: Enables printing the disassembly before each pass and after the last pass to the given output stream. If out is null, printing is disabled.
requirements: If out is non-null, it must remain valid for the duration of Run() calls that print.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::SetTimeReport
functions.description: Enables reporting resource utilization of each pass to the given stream. If out is null, reporting is disabled.
requirements: If out is non-null, it must remain valid for the duration of Run() calls that report.

functions.name: spvtools::Optimizer::SetValidateAfterAll
functions.description: Controls whether to validate the module after each pass.
requirements: None. Set to true to enable per-pass validation; may impact compile time.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateNullPass
functions.description: Creates a pass token for a null pass that performs no transformations.
requirements: None.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateStripDebugInfoPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes all debug instructions per SPIR-V spec section 3.42.2.
requirements: Module should be valid SPIR-V; debug instructions will be stripped.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateStripReflectInfoPass
functions.description: Deprecated. Creates a pass equivalent to strip-nonsemantic-info.
requirements: Prefer CreateStripNonSemanticInfoPass in new code.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateStripNonSemanticInfoPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes reflection and explicitly non-semantic instructions.
requirements: Module should be valid SPIR-V.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateEliminateDeadFunctionsPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes functions not reachable from entry points or exported functions.
requirements: Functions removed must not be in call trees rooted at entry points or exports.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateEliminateDeadMembersPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes unused struct members without changing the layout of remaining members.
requirements: Only unused members are removed; remaining members keep data layout.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateSetSpecConstantDefaultValuePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that sets default values for SpecId-decorated specialization constants using string representations.
requirements: id_value_map keys are SpecId values of OpSpecConstant{,True,False}.
String values must be parseable to the target constant types.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateSetSpecConstantDefaultValuePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that sets default values for SpecId-decorated specialization constants using raw bit patterns.
requirements: id_value_map keys are SpecId values of OpSpecConstant{,True,False}.
Bit patterns must match the target constant types' sizes and encodings.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateFlattenDecorationPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that replaces grouped decorations (OpDecorationGroup, OpGroupDecorate, OpGroupMemberDecorate) with equivalent ungrouped decorations (OpDecorate, OpMemberDecorate).
requirements: Debug info for removed instructions is not preserved.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateFreezeSpecConstantValuePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that specializes SpecId specialization constants to their default values, replacing them with normal constants. Does not fold further or handle composite/op spec constants.
requirements: Only affects OpSpecConstant{,True,False} with SpecId decorations.
Does not process OpSpecConstantComposite or OpSpecConstantOp.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateFoldSpecConstantOpAndCompositePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that folds OpSpecConstantOp and OpSpecConstantComposite into equivalent normal constants when values are determinable. Some operations (e.g., OpSConvert, OpFConvert, OpQuantizeToF16, and all Kernel capability ops) are not supported.
requirements: Only folds when all operand values are determinable from the module.
Unsupported operations are left unchanged.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateUnifyConstantPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that de-duplicates constants with identical types and values. Certain cases (null vs zero, decorated constants, NaN bit-pattern variants) are not unified.
requirements: Constants with decorations on result ids are not unified.
Null and zero-valued constants are not considered equivalent.
NaNs with different bit patterns are not unified.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateEliminateDeadConstantPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes dead constants (normal and spec constants) not used by the module.
requirements: Removes constants defined by OpConstant{,Composite,True,False} and OpSpecConstant*, including OpSpecConstantOp, when dead.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateStrengthReductionPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that replaces expensive instructions with equivalent cheaper ones (e.g., multiply by power of 2 -> shift).
requirements: None.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateBlockMergePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that merges a block with a single branch to a block with no other predecessors into a single block, excluding merge/continue blocks. Helps after dead-branch elimination.
requirements: Presence of phi instructions can inhibit merging.
Does not guarantee elimination of all candidates.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateInlineExhaustivePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that attempts to inline all function calls reachable from entry points, enabling cross-function optimizations. Not size/performance optimized.
requirements: Only functions in entry-point call trees are affected.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateInlineOpaquePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that inlines calls where the callee has an opaque type (Image, Sampler, SampledImage) in parameters or return type, to enable legality for Vulkan.
requirements: Only functions in entry-point call trees are affected.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateLocalSingleBlockLoadStoreElimPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that performs single-block local variable load/store elimination for function variables referenced only via non-access-chain loads/stores.
requirements: Only modules with relaxed logical addressing are processed.
Access chains and function calls can inhibit optimization.
Only functions in entry-point call trees are processed.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateDeadBranchElimPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes branches with constant conditions and deletes resulting dead blocks. Updates phis in merge blocks accordingly.
requirements: Some branches/blocks may be retained to preserve valid control flow.
Most effective after local load/store elimination.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateLocalMultiStoreElimPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that eliminates loads/stores of function-scope variables referenced only with non-access-chain loads/stores, and removes the variables.
requirements: Only shader modules with relaxed logical addressing are processed.
Currently modules with any extensions enabled are not processed.
Access chains and function calls can inhibit optimization.
Preceding passes (Inlining, LocalAccessChainConvert, LocalSingleStoreElim/LocalSingleBlockElim) improve results.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateLocalAccessChainConvertPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that converts accesses to function-scope variables using access chains with constant indices into equivalent loads/stores/extracts/inserts.
requirements: Processes only entry-point functions.
Converts only non-nested, non-pointer access chains.
Does not process modules with non-32-bit integer types present.
Ignores optional memory access operands on loads/stores for function-scope variables.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateLocalSingleStoreElimPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes loads/stores for function-scope variables stored exactly once (whole-variable accesses only), replacing loads with the stored value and removing dead code.
requirements: Only shader modules with relaxed logical addressing are processed.
Access chains and function calls can inhibit optimization; preceding inlining and access-chain conversion improve results.
Many non-load/store memory ops are not supported and will prohibit optimization of a function.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateInsertExtractElimPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes extracts when a prior insert with matching indices supplies the value, enabling subsequent dead code elimination of inserts.
requirements: Works best after access chains are converted and local load/store elimination.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateDeadInsertElimPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes unreferenced inserts into composite types and attempts DCE on inserted values.
requirements: Best after access chain conversion and local load/store elimination, and after InsertExtractElim.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateAggressiveDCEPass
functions.description: Creates an aggressive DCE pass that removes unused code and some code with spurious uses that do not contribute to function outputs. Processes only entry points and shaders with relaxed logical addressing; currently not functions with calls. Unreachable functions are deleted.
requirements: Only processes entry-point functions.
Only processes shaders with relaxed logical addressing.
Currently will not process functions with function calls.
More effective after removing dead control flow and inlining.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateAggressiveDCEPass
functions.description: Same as aggressive DCE, but preserves all non-IO variables in the entry point interface if preserve_interface is true (required for some validation tooling).
requirements: If preserve_interface is true, interface variables are considered live and not eliminated.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateAggressiveDCEPass
functions.description: Aggressive DCE with controls to preserve interface variables and optionally remove outputs from the interface when safe.
requirements: If preserve_interface is true, interface variables are preserved.
If remove_outputs is true, caller must ensure there is no corresponding input variable in the following shader; otherwise interface mismatch may occur.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateRemoveUnusedInterfaceVariablesPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes variables listed on OpEntryPoint that are not actually referenced in the entry point call tree. May change the shader interface.
requirements: May cause interface to not match other pipeline stages; use with care.

functions.name: spvtools::CreatePropagateLineInfoPass
functions.description: Creates a deprecated empty pass kept temporarily for compatibility.
requirements: Deprecated; scheduled for removal.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateRedundantLineInfoElimPass
functions.description: Creates a deprecated empty pass kept temporarily for compatibility.
requirements: Deprecated; scheduled for removal.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateCompactIdsPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that remaps result ids to a compact, gapless range starting at %1.
requirements: None.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateRemoveDuplicatesPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes duplicates of capabilities, extended instruction imports, types, and decorations.
requirements: None.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateCFGCleanupPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes cruft from control-flow graphs of reachable functions, including unreachable blocks.
requirements: Operates on functions reachable from entry points or exported functions.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateDeadVariableEliminationPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that deletes unreferenced module-scope variables and their decorations.
requirements: Only variables that are not referenced are removed.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateMergeReturnPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that rewrites functions with multiple return statements to use a single return. Assumes only unreachable blocks are trivial merge/continue blocks, which is guaranteed after dead-branch elimination.
requirements: Run after dead-branch elimination to satisfy assumptions about trivial merge/continue blocks.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateLocalRedundancyEliminationPass
functions.description: Creates a value numbering pass that removes redundant computations within the same basic block.
requirements: None.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateLoopInvariantCodeMotionPass
functions.description: Creates a LICM pass that hoists loop-invariant instructions to the loop preheader.
requirements: None.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateLoopFissionPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that splits top-level loops whose estimated register pressure exceeds the given threshold.
requirements: threshold should be a sensible non-negative limit for register pressure.
Only top-level loops are considered.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateLoopFusionPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that fuses compatible adjacent loops as long as the fused loop stays below max_registers_per_loop.
requirements: max_registers_per_loop should be a sensible non-negative limit.
Only compatible and legal loops are fused.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateLoopPeelingPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that peels iterations when a loop has conditions that are true/false only for the first or last N iterations, limiting code growth by an internal threshold.
requirements: Loop peeling occurs only if code growth stays under an internal code_growth_threshold.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateLoopUnswitchPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that moves loop-invariant branch conditions outside the loop (unswitching), potentially versioning the loop. Works best after LICM and local multi-store elimination.
requirements: More effective after LICM and LocalMultiStoreElim.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateRedundancyEliminationPass
functions.description: Creates a global value numbering pass that removes instructions computing the same value on all incoming paths.
requirements: None.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateScalarReplacementPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that replaces composite function-scope variables with per-element variables when accessed individually. size_limit bounds the number of members considered.
requirements: size_limit is a limit on composite members to consider; 0 means default behavior as implemented.

functions.name: spvtools::CreatePrivateToLocalPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that moves variables from Private storage class to Function storage class when used in only one function.
requirements: Only variables used in exactly one function are moved.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateCCPPass
functions.description: Creates a Conditional Constant Propagation (SSA-CCP) pass, folding constant expressions and simplifying conditional jumps per Wegman-Zadeck algorithm.
requirements: Best results when dead code is already minimized.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateWorkaround1209Pass
functions.description: Creates a pass that rewrites code to avoid known driver bug #1209; currently removes OpUnreachable in loops.
requirements: Has effect only when such problematic patterns exist.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateIfConversionPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that converts if-then-else-like assignments into OpSelect operations.
requirements: Conditional structure must match recognizable assignment patterns to convert.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateReplaceInvalidOpcodePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that replaces instructions invalid for the current shader stage with constants. No effect on non-shader modules.
requirements: Module must declare a shader stage for there to be an effect.
Invalid opcodes for the stage are replaced with constants.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateSimplificationPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that simplifies instructions using the instruction folder (constant folding and algebraic simplifications).
requirements: None.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateLoopUnrollPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that unrolls loops with the Unroll loop control, subject to LoopUtils::CanPerformUnroll. If fully_unroll is true, performs full unroll; otherwise uses 'factor' if > 0.
requirements: Only loops that satisfy LoopUtils::CanPerformUnroll are unrolled.
factor should be a positive integer when partial unrolling is requested.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateSSARewritePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that converts eligible function-local variables from load/store form into SSA IDs to enable SSA optimizations.
requirements: Only variables local to the function and of supported types are processed (per IsSSATargetVar).

functions.name: spvtools::CreateConvertRelaxedToHalfPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that converts as many relaxed float32 arithmetic operations as possible to float16, inserting necessary conversions to/from float32. Does not change variables or image ops.
requirements: Best run after store/load and composite op eliminations and before simplification, redundancy elimination, and DCE.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateRelaxFloatOpsPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that decorates float32 result instructions with RelaxedPrecision if not already decorated.
requirements: Applies only to float32 result instructions.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateCopyPropagateArraysPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that recognizes array copy patterns and propagates array references to eliminate redundant copies.
requirements: Pattern-based; only recognized array copy forms are optimized.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateVectorDCEPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes unused components from vectors; follow-up ADCE may be needed to remove remaining dead code.
requirements: Only unused vector components are removed.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateReduceLoadSizePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that replaces loads of composites (e.g., structs) with narrower loads (via access chains) when only some members are used, if the used-to-total ratio is below the given threshold.
requirements: load_replacement_threshold must be in [0,1] for meaningful behavior.
Only loads feeding OpExtract-like uses are considered.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateCombineAccessChainsPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that combines chained OpAccessChain instructions into a single access chain where possible.
requirements: Combines only when legal and does not change semantics.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateUpgradeMemoryModelPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that upgrades the Logical GLSL450 memory model to Logical VulkanKHR and adjusts memory/image/atomic/barrier operations accordingly.
requirements: Module should target an environment where VulkanKHR memory model is applicable.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateCodeSinkingPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that moves instructions into more deeply nested constructs when profitable (code sinking).
requirements: Moves only when legal for dominance and side-effect constraints.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateFixStorageClassPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that fixes certain incorrect storage classes commonly produced by DXC to simplify code generation.
requirements: Only storage class mismatches that the pass recognizes are fixed.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateGraphicsRobustAccessPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that clamps indexed buffer and internal array accesses to satisfy Vulkan robustBufferAccess rules. Also addresses some image texel pointer cases.
requirements: Module must be a Shader module.
Must not declare VariablePointers, VariablePointersStorageBuffer, or RuntimeDescriptorArrayEXT capabilities.
Addressing model must be Logical.
Access chain indices must be ≤ 64 bits wide.
Struct access indices must be OpConstant integers and in-range.
ImageTexelPointer coordinate components must be 32-bit (TODO notes an assumption).
Indices are treated as signed; very large arrays may clamp indices into signed range.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateSpreadVolatileSemanticsPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that spreads Volatile semantics to variables or loads of certain BuiltIns (e.g., SMIDNV, WarpIDNV, Subgroup* masks) in specific ray-tracing shader models; also applies to HelperInvocation in fragment shader for SPIR-V 1.6+.
requirements: Module shader model must be one of: ray generation, closest hit, miss, intersection, or callable for the listed BuiltIns.
For SPIR-V 1.6+, spreads to HelperInvocation BuiltIn in fragment shader.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateReplaceDescArrayAccessUsingVarIndexPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that replaces variable-indexed accesses to descriptor array variables with constant element accesses via a generated switch.
requirements: Target variable must have DescriptorSet and Binding decorations to be transformed.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateDescriptorScalarReplacementPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that replaces each descriptor array/composite with separate variables per element, remapping bindings so that element i uses binding b+i. Flattens both composites and arrays.
requirements: Original variable must have DescriptorSet and Binding decorations.
Assumes no other variable already uses any of the new bindings; otherwise the result may be invalid SPIR-V.
All accesses must be OpAccessChain with a literal constant for the first index.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateDescriptorCompositeScalarReplacementPass
functions.description: Creates a pass like descriptor scalar replacement but only flattens composites.
requirements: Same as descriptor scalar replacement, limited to composites.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateDescriptorArrayScalarReplacementPass
functions.description: Creates a pass like descriptor scalar replacement but only flattens arrays.
requirements: Same as descriptor scalar replacement, limited to arrays.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateWrapOpKillPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that replaces OpKill and OpTerminateInvocation with calls to wrapper functions containing those instructions, enabling more inlining.
requirements: Module must contain OpKill and/or OpTerminateInvocation to have effect.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateAmdExtToKhrPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that replaces VK_AMD_shader_ballot, VK_AMD_gcn_shader, and VK_AMD_shader_trinary_minmax with equivalent core instructions and capabilities.
requirements: Module must use those AMD extensions to have effect.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateInterpolateFixupPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that replaces internal GLSLstd450 InterpolateAt* variants (which take OpLoad of the interpolant) with the externally-valid form using the pointer directly. Intended for HLSL legalization.
requirements: Run after interpolants have been propagated to final positions.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateOpExtInstWithForwardReferenceFixupPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that converts between OpExtInst and OpExtInstWithForwardRefsKHR depending on whether the instruction references a forward-declared debug instruction.
requirements: Affects only debug extended instruction cases with/without forward references.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateEliminateDeadInputComponentsPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes unused components from composite input variables (currently trailing elements of arrays and structs). Best after aggressive DCE. WARNING: Safe standalone only for vertex shaders; may cause interface mismatches otherwise.
requirements: Apply to vertex shaders standalone. For other stages, follow pipeline-safe sequence (see notes about dead output stores/components).

functions.name: spvtools::CreateEliminateDeadOutputComponentsPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes unused components from composite output variables (currently trailing elements) for vertex and fragment shaders. Best after eliminating dead output stores.
requirements: Supports only vertex and fragment shaders.
Not safe standalone; ensure compatibility with following shader by first applying appropriate input/output passes as documented.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateEliminateDeadInputComponentsSafePass
functions.description: Creates a safe variant removing unused components from input variables without causing interface incompatibilities by limiting changes to vertex shaders.
requirements: Safe standalone because it changes only vertex shaders.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateAnalyzeLiveInputPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that analyzes a shader and populates live input locations and builtins for use by dead output store elimination in the preceding shader. Supports tessellation control/evaluation, geometry, and fragment shaders.
requirements: live_locs must be a valid non-null pointer to a set to receive location ids.
live_builtins must be a valid non-null pointer to a set to receive builtin ids.
Best results after eliminating dead code.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateEliminateDeadOutputStoresPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes stores to output locations not listed in the provided live sets. Best after constant propagation; follow with ADCE and dead output component elimination. Supports vertex, tessellation control/evaluation, and geometry shaders.
requirements: live_locs must be a valid non-null pointer containing live output locations.
live_builtins must be a valid non-null pointer containing live builtins.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateConvertToSampledImagePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that converts images and/or samplers with specified (set,binding) pairs into sampled images. Also converts images alone with a matched pair.
requirements: descriptor_set_binding_pairs must list valid descriptor set/binding pairs to be converted.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateInterfaceVariableScalarReplacementPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that replaces array/matrix interface variables with multiple scalar/vector interface variables (e.g., float3 foo[2] -> float3 foo0, foo1).
requirements: May change the shader interface; ensure pipeline compatibility.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateRemoveDontInlinePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes the DontInline function control from all functions to allow inlining.
requirements: Module must contain functions with DontInline to have effect.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateFixFuncCallArgumentsPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that fixes non-memory arguments for function calls to satisfy SPIR-V validation (e.g., removing access-chain pointer arguments).
requirements: Targets cases where SPIR-V requires memory object parameters for function calls.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateTrimCapabilitiesPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that removes unused capabilities and, when possible, associated extensions. See trim_capabilities.h for supported capabilities.
requirements: Unsupported capabilities are ignored; results may be imperfect if unknown capabilities interact with trimmed ones.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateStructPackingPass
functions.signature: spvtools::Optimizer::PassToken spvtools::CreateStructPackingPass(const char* structToPack, const char* packingRule)
functions.description: Creates a pass that reassigns Offset decorations to tightly pack the named struct according to a specified packing rule (std140, std140EnhancedLayout, std430, std430EnhancedLayout, hlslCbuffer, hlslCbufferPackOffset, scalar, scalarEnhancedLayout).
requirements: structToPack must be the OpName of the target struct.
packingRule must be one of the accepted rule identifiers listed.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateSwitchDescriptorSetPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that changes DescriptorSet decorations with value ds_from to ds_to.
requirements: ds_from and ds_to are descriptor set numbers to be remapped.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateInvocationInterlockPlacementPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that ensures each entry point has at most one OpBeginInterlockInvocationEXT and one OpEndInterlockInvocationEXT, in order.
requirements: Module must target an environment supporting the interlock extension/modes for changes to be valid.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateModifyMaximalReconvergencePass
functions.description: Creates a pass that adds or removes the MaximalReconvergence execution mode on all entry points.
requirements: add determines whether to add (true) or remove (false) the mode.
Target environment must support the execution mode when adding.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateSplitCombinedImageSamplerPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that splits combined image+sampler variables and parameters into separate image and sampler components, copying bindings and decorations.
requirements: Module must contain combined image+sampler constructs to have effect.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateResolveBindingConflictsPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that remaps bindings to avoid conflicts in Vulkan-valid modules when distinct variables share the same (set,binding) at an entry point. Sampler-vs-image conflicts are resolved by incrementing sampler bindings and propagating increments.
requirements: Assumes bindings are not applied via OpDecorationGroup.
Module must be valid for Vulkan for the conflict definition to apply.

functions.name: spvtools::CreateCanonicalizeIdsPass
functions.description: Creates a pass that canonicalizes IDs to improve cross-module compression of SPIR-V binaries. Increases ID range but improves compressor dictionary sharing. Run near the end and before strip-debug, since OpName is used.
requirements: Run most other optimization passes first; run --strip-debug after this pass if desired.

functions.name: spvtools::LinkerOptions::GetCreateLibrary
functions.description: Returns whether the linker should produce a library (true) or an executable (false). Intended to guide the linking phase about keeping exported symbols (library) versus stripping them (executable).

functions.name: spvtools::LinkerOptions::SetCreateLibrary

functions.description: Links one or more SPIR-V modules (provided as a vector of word-vectors) into a single SPIR-V module. Produces the linked binary in linked_binary. Use when all inputs are already in-memory as std::vector<uint32_t> modules.
requirements: > context must be a valid SPIR-V Tools context initialized via spvContextCreate().
> binaries must contain at least one module.
> Each module in binaries must be parseable SPIR-V (validity is not strictly required).
> All input modules must agree on addressing and memory models.
> The resulting ID or global variable number limits must not be exceeded.
> Entry points must not be defined multiple times across inputs.
> If partial linkage is not allowed (per options), all imported symbols must have exported counterparts.
> linked_binary must be a non-null pointer to a writable std::vector<uint32_t> to receive the result.
> Function may fail for the documented reasons (and possibly others) and will return a spv_result_t indicating success or failure.

import random

# This generator targets inputs for functions that consume generic text strings:
# - spvParseTargetEnv expects a C string naming a SPIR-V target environment.
# - spvDiagnosticCreate uses an arbitrary message string.
# We produce a bytes buffer which the fuzzing framework will split to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# and other consumers. We bias toward valid environment names to exercise success paths,
# but also include a variety of tricky and invalid strings to exercise failure paths.

_VALID_ENV_STRINGS = [
    # Canonical names commonly accepted by SPIRV-Tools parser
    "spv1.0",
    "spv1.1",
    "spv1.2",
    "spv1.3",
    "spv1.4",
    "spv1.5",
    "spv1.6",
    "vulkan1.0",
    "vulkan1.1",
    "vulkan1.1.spirv1.4",
    "vulkan1.2",
    "vulkan1.3",
    "vulkan1.4",
    "opengl4.0",
    "opengl4.1",
    "opengl4.2",
    "opengl4.3",
    "opengl4.5",
    "opencl1.2",
    "opencl2.0",
    "opencl2.1",
    "opencl2.2",
    "opencl-embedded1.2",
    "opencl-embedded2.0",
    "opencl-embedded2.1",
    "opencl-embedded2.2",
    "webgpu0",
    # Enum-like spellings sometimes accepted
    "universal-1.0",
    "universal-1.1",
    "universal-1.2",
    "universal-1.3",
    "universal-1.4",
    "universal-1.5",
    "universal-1.6",
]

# Additional interesting strings to probe parser robustness and general text handling
_EDGE_CASE_STRINGS = [
    "",  # empty
    " ",
    "\t\n",
    "unrecognized-env",
    "VULKAN1.2",      # case variant
    "SpV1.3",         # mixed case
    "vulkan1.1.spirv1.4\0extra",  # embedded NUL notion; will be cut at first NUL by C APIs
    "vulkan1.2 --flag",
    "opencl2.0\n",
    "spv1.5#comment",
    "universal-1.6,extra",
]

def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " \t\n"
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

def _pick_env_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Bias: 70% valid, 30% edge/random
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.7:
        s = rng.choice(_VALID_ENV_STRINGS)
        # Occasionally introduce benign whitespace padding that C parser might trim/handle
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            left = "" if rng.random() < 0.5 else " " * rng.randint(1, 3)
            right = "" if rng.random() < 0.5 else rng.choice([" ", "\n", "\t"]) * rng.randint(1, 2)
            s = left + s + right
        return s
    elif roll < 0.9:
        return rng.choice(_EDGE_CASE_STRINGS)
    else:
        return _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 32)

def _build_c_string_block(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create several concatenated NUL-terminated strings so multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    # can consume distinct inputs. Keep total size <= 4 KiB.
    parts = []
    # First: an environment string
    parts.append(_pick_env_string(rng))
    # Second: a general message string for diagnostics, often multi-line and with punctuation
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        msg = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 128)
    else:
        msg = rng.choice([
            "OK",
            "warning: unused variable x",
            "error: invalid opcode",
            "info: validated successfully",
            "debug: path=a/b/c id=42",
            "🚀 unicode rocket",  # Unicode; will be UTF-8 encoded
        ])
    parts.append(msg)
    # Additional miscellaneous strings to diversify consumption
    extra_count = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for _ in range(extra_count):
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 0, 64))
    # Join with NUL terminators; ensure final NUL present
    blob = b"".join((p.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00") for p in parts)
    return blob

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    blob = _build_c_string_block(rng)
    # Enforce size limit
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]
        # Ensure the buffer ends with a NUL so the last C string is properly terminated
        if not blob.endswith(b"\x00"):
            # Replace last byte with NUL to avoid unterminated tail
            blob = blob[:-1] + b"\x00"
    return blob

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces SPIR-V assembly text (UTF-8) as bytes.
# It aims to create mostly-valid, interesting modules that exercise:
# - spvTextToBinary(WithOptions)
# - spvtools::SpirvTools::Assemble / Parse / Disassemble / Validate
# We vary target environment via capabilities/versions, include optional extensions,
# multiple entry points, functions, control flow, types, constants, composites, decorations,
# execution modes, and various instructions across shader stages.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

def _rand_name(r: random.Random, prefix: str) -> str:
    return f"{prefix}{r.randint(0, 1<<16):x}"

def _choose(r: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[r.randrange(len(items))]

def _maybe(r: random.Random, p: float) -> bool:
    return r.random() < p

def _header_universal(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Randomly choose SPIR-V version guard via Capability + MemoryModel
    versions = [
        ("1.0", ["Shader"], "Logical", "GLSL450"),
        ("1.3", ["Shader"], "Logical", "GLSL450"),
        ("1.5", ["Shader"], "Logical", "GLSL450"),
        ("1.6", ["Shader"], "Logical", "GLSL450"),
    ]
    ver, caps, addressing, mem = _choose(r, versions)
    lines = []
    lines.append(f"; SPIR-V\n; Version: {ver}\n; Generator: 0\n; Bound: 200\n; Schema: 0")
    for c in caps:
        lines.append(f"OpCapability {c}")
    # Occasionally add extra capabilities to open code paths.
    extra_caps = [
        "Int8", "Int16", "Int64", "Float16", "Float64", "Vector16",
        "Matrix", "Linkage", "UniformAndStorageBuffer8BitAccess",
        "StorageBuffer8BitAccess", "StorageUniform16", "Int64Atomics",
    ]
    if _maybe(r, 0.5):
        for c in r.sample(extra_caps, r.randint(0, min(3, len(extra_caps)))):
            lines.append(f"OpCapability {c}")
    # Optional extensions commonly accepted
    ext_pool = [
        "SPV_KHR_storage_buffer_storage_class",
        "SPV_KHR_vulkan_memory_model",
        "SPV_KHR_shader_draw_parameters",
        "SPV_EXT_descriptor_indexing",
        "SPV_KHR_non_semantic_info",
    ]
    if _maybe(r, 0.4):
        for e in r.sample(ext_pool, r.randint(1, min(2, len(ext_pool)))):
            lines.append(f"OpExtension \"{e}\"")
    lines.append("OpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def _common_types_and_consts(r: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = []
    # Basic types
    lines += [
        "%void = OpTypeVoid",
        "%bool = OpTypeBool",
        "%i32 = OpTypeInt 32 1",
        "%u32 = OpTypeInt 32 0",
        "%f32 = OpTypeFloat 32",
        "%v2f = OpTypeVector %f32 2",
        "%v3f = OpTypeVector %f32 3",
        "%v4f = OpTypeVector %f32 4",
        "%m2 = OpTypeMatrix %v2f 2",
        "%m3 = OpTypeMatrix %v3f 3",
        "%voidfn = OpTypeFunction %void",
        "%fun_i = OpTypeFunction %i32",
        "%fun_v = OpTypeFunction %void",
    ]
    # Pointers (Storage Classes vary per stage later). We'll declare a few common.
    lines += [
        "%ptr_pu32 = OpTypePointer PushConstant %u32",
        "%ptr_fu32 = OpTypePointer Function %u32",
        "%ptr_ff32 = OpTypePointer Function %f32",
        "%ptr_in_v4f = OpTypePointer Input %v4f",
        "%ptr_out_v4f = OpTypePointer Output %v4f",
    ]
    # Constants
    c_vals = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 255, 1024]
    for v in c_vals:
        lines.append(f"%u{v} = OpConstant %u32 {v}")
    lines += [
        "%i_1 = OpConstant %i32 1",
        "%i_2 = OpConstant %i32 2",
        "%f_0 = OpConstant %f32 0.0",
        "%f_1 = OpConstant %f32 1.0",
        "%f_2 = OpConstant %f32 2.0",
    ]
    # Composite constants
    lines += [
        "%c_v4f1 = OpConstantComposite %v4f %f_1 %f_1 %f_1 %f_1",
        "%c_v4f2 = OpConstantComposite %v4f %f_2 %f_2 %f_2 %f_2",
    ]
    # Structures
    lines += [
        "%S = OpTypeStruct %v4f",
        "%ptr_ssbo_S = OpTypePointer StorageBuffer %S",
    ]
    # Uniform/storage variables
    lines += [
        "%out_color = OpVariable %ptr_out_v4f Output",
    ]
    # Decorations
    lines += [
        "OpDecorate %out_color Location 0",
        "OpMemberDecorate %S 0 Offset 0",
        "OpDecorate %S Block",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines)

def _make_entry_vertex(r: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = []
    lines.append("OpEntryPoint Vertex %main_v \"main_v\" %out_color")
    lines.append("OpExecutionMode %main_v OriginUpperLeft")
    lines.append("%main_v = OpFunction %void None %voidfn")
    lines.append("%l0 = OpLabel")
    # Simple arithmetic and composite ops
    lines.append("%t0 = OpFAdd %f32 %f_1 %f_2")
    lines.append("%t1 = OpCompositeConstruct %v4f %t0 %f_1 %f_2 %f_0")
    lines.append("OpStore %out_color %t1")
    lines.append("OpReturn")
    lines.append("OpFunctionEnd")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def _make_entry_fragment(r: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = []
    lines.append("OpEntryPoint Fragment %main_f \"main_f\" %out_color")
    lines.append("OpExecutionMode %main_f OriginUpperLeft")
    lines.append("%main_f = OpFunction %void None %voidfn")
    lines.append("%fl = OpLabel")
    # Conditional and vector ops
    lines.append("%cond = OpSLessThan %bool %i_1 %i_2")
    lines.append("%sel = OpSelect %v4f %cond %c_v4f1 %c_v4f2")
    lines.append("OpStore %out_color %sel")
    lines.append("OpReturn")
    lines.append("OpFunctionEnd")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def _make_extra_funcs(r: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = []
    if _maybe(r, 0.7):
        # A helper function returning i32
        lines.append("%fn_add = OpFunction %i32 None %fun_i")
        lines.append("%bl = OpLabel")
        lines.append("%a = OpIAdd %i32 %i_1 %i_2")
        lines.append("OpReturnValue %a")
        lines.append("OpFunctionEnd")
    if _maybe(r, 0.5):
        # A void function with loop-like control flow (minimal)
        lines.append("%fn_void = OpFunction %void None %voidfn")
        lines.append("%lb = OpLabel")
        lines.append("OpBranch %bb1")
        lines.append("%bb1 = OpLabel")
        lines.append("OpReturn")
        lines.append("OpFunctionEnd")
    return "\n".join(lines)

def _module(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    parts.append(_header_universal(r))
    parts.append(_common_types_and_consts(r))
    # Entry points: choose 1-2 stages
    stages = []
    if _maybe(r, 0.8):
        stages.append(_make_entry_vertex(r))
    if _maybe(r, 0.8):
        stages.append(_make_entry_fragment(r))
    if not stages:
        stages.append(_make_entry_vertex(r))
    parts.extend(stages)
    parts.append(_make_extra_funcs(r))
    return "\n".join(p for p in parts if p)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose one of several templates to diversify instruction coverage
    asm = _module(r)

    # Occasionally spice with friendly OpName and extra decorations to impact options
    extras = []
    if _maybe(r, 0.7):
        for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)):
            nm = _rand_name(r, "id_")
            extras.append(f"OpName %out_color \"{nm}\"")
    if extras:
        asm = asm + "\n" + "\n".join(extras)

    # Ensure size limit
    data = asm.encode("utf-8")
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
        data = data[:MAX_BYTES]
    return data

    # Bias toward valid assembly snippets; occasionally return binary bytes payload.
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.85:
        txt = rng.choice(_SPV_VALID_SNIPPETS)
        # Randomly add or omit the header comments; the assembler accepts either.
        prefix = rng.choice(_DEF_PREFIXES)
        return (prefix + txt)[:4096]
    else:
        # Return a compact raw-bytes payload. The stub will try Assemble first; if it
        # fails, it will pack these bytes into words as a fallback binary.
        # We randomize between the embedded minimal valid binary and slight variants
        # by appending padding bytes so size/word-count varies (still valid header-first).
        pad_len = rng.randint(0, 16)
        payload = _MINIMAL_VALID_BINARY_LE + bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(pad_len))
        return payload[:4096].decode('latin1', errors='ignore')

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    text_or_bytes = _choose_snippet(rng)
    # FUZZ_PARAM_STR returns std::string; here we provide bytes. Use UTF-8 encoding
    # while preserving arbitrary bytes for fallback case via latin1 when needed.
    try:
        data = text_or_bytes.encode('utf-8')
    except Exception:
        data = text_or_bytes.encode('latin1', errors='ignore')
    # Ensure non-empty to avoid guard paths skipping pointer overloads elsewhere.
    if not data:
        data = b"OpCapability Shader\nOpMemoryModel Logical GLSL450\n"
    return data[:4096]

from typing import List

# Target: Generate interesting CSV strings (and small filename-like paths) for
# spvtools::LinkerOptions setters that expect CSV-likes and file lists.
# The fuzzer stubs:
# - Use FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for CSV strings (targets/architectures)
# - Use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() for file paths
# Our single bytes buffer will be consumed by the fuzzer to derive both kinds.
# We'll therefore encode multiple candidate CSV strings and filenames in one
# buffer, separated by NULs. Common fuzz harnesses pick sequentially or by
# slicing; NULs are a safe separator.
#
# Design:
# - Construct 4-8 CSV strings covering edge cases:
#   * empty
#   * single token
#   * multiple tokens
#   * tokens with spaces, quotes, escapes
#   * long tokens near the 512 trim limit
#   * tokens containing commas already
#   * Unicode/symbol tokens (valid UTF-8)
# - Construct 0-3 filename-like entries: absolute, relative, with extension,
#   nested dirs. No actual I/O will occur; just strings.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Randomize order/content seeded by input.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

TOK_SIMPLE = [
    "target", "arch", "sm_50", "sm_75", "gfx1010", "gfx1100",
    "v1", "v1.1", "v1.2", "spirv1.0", "spirv1.6", "vulkan1.0",
]
TOK_WITH_SYMS = [
    "x-y", "a_b", "arm64", "x86_64", "riscv64", "wasm32",
    "shader+compute", "glsl450", "opengl4.5", "dxc-hlsl",
]
TOK_WITH_SPACES = [
    "my target", "my arch", "feature set A", "capability all",
]
TOK_WITH_QUOTES = [
    '"quoted"', "'single'", '\\escaped', 'name="val"', "k=v",
]
TOK_UNICODE = [
    "μarch", "βeta", "спираль", "連結", "リンク", "δοκιμή",
]

def rand_csv(rng: random.Random, target_len_hint: int) -> str:
    # Choose a style
    styles = ["empty", "single", "multi", "spaces", "quotes", "unicode", "long"]
    style = rng.choice(styles)
    if style == "empty":
        return ""
    if style == "single":
        pool = TOK_SIMPLE + TOK_WITH_SYMS + TOK_UNICODE
        return rng.choice(pool)
    if style == "multi":
        pool = TOK_SIMPLE + TOK_WITH_SYMS
        n = rng.randint(2, 8)
        parts = rng.choices(pool, k=n)
        return ",".join(parts)
    if style == "spaces":
        pool = TOK_WITH_SPACES + TOK_SIMPLE
        n = rng.randint(2, 6)
        parts = rng.choices(pool, k=n)
        return ",".join(parts)
    if style == "quotes":
        pool = TOK_WITH_QUOTES + TOK_SIMPLE
        n = rng.randint(2, 6)
        parts = rng.choices(pool, k=n)
        return ",".join(parts)
    if style == "unicode":
        pool = TOK_UNICODE + TOK_SIMPLE
        n = rng.randint(2, 6)
        parts = rng.choices(pool, k=n)
        return ",".join(parts)
    # long
    # Build a long tokenized string near 512 chars (trim threshold in stub)
    base_pool = TOK_SIMPLE + TOK_WITH_SYMS
    s = []
    while len(",".join(s)) < max(256, target_len_hint):
        tok_len = rng.randint(3, 12)
        tok = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_") for _ in range(tok_len))
        s.append(tok)
    return ",".join(s)[:rng.randint(100, 520)]

def rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose between absolute and relative paths. No actual FS access needed.
    prefixes = ["/tmp/", "/var/tmp/", "./", "../", "C:/temp/", "D:/work/"]
    prefix = rng.choice(prefixes)
    parts = []
    depth = rng.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        name_len = rng.randint(1, 8)
        name = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_") for _ in range(name_len))
        parts.append(name)
    base_len = rng.randint(1, 10)
    base = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_") for _ in range(base_len))
    exts = [".spv", ".bin", ".spirv", ".dat", ".tmp"]
    ext = rng.choice(exts)
    path_mid = "/".join(parts + [base]) if parts else base
    return f"{prefix}{path_mid}{ext}"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build multiple CSV strings first; include ones tuned for both SetFnVarTargetsCsv and SetFnVarArchitecturesCsv
    csvs: List[str] = []
    count_csv = rng.randint(4, 8)
    for _ in range(count_csv):
        # Provide varying target length hints around 512 to exercise trimming and commas insertion logic
        hint = rng.choice([64, 128, 256, 400, 512, 600])
        s = rand_csv(rng, hint)
        # Ensure at least one entry has no comma (so stub injects one)
        if rng.random() < 0.3 and s and "," in s:
            # collapse to first token to create a no-comma case
            s = s.split(",")[0]
        csvs.append(s)

    # Build a few filenames for SetInFiles
    filenames: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        filenames.append(rand_filename(rng))

    # Also include a couple of obviously CSV-looking canonical examples
    csvs.extend([
        "compute,graphics,link,legalize",
        "x86_64,arm64,riscv64",
    ])

    # Compose the final buffer: NUL-separated strings where the harness can pick sequentially.
    # Order them alternating to increase variety on early pulls.
    pieces: List[str] = []
    interleave = []
    # Interleave csv and filenames a bit
    fi = 0
    for ci, c in enumerate(csvs):
        interleave.append(c)
        if fi < len(filenames) and rng.random() < 0.5:
            interleave.append(filenames[fi])
            fi += 1
    while fi < len(filenames):
        interleave.append(filenames[fi])
        fi += 1

    # Join with NULs and ensure under size limit
    data = ("\x00".join(interleave)).encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
        # Ensure we end on a boundary to not cut UTF-8 mid-sequence too badly; trim to last NUL if possible
        last_nul = data.rfind(b"\x00")
        if last_nul > 0:
            data = data[:last_nul]
    return data

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filename path
# The stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to obtain a path to a fuzzer-created file
# and FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for CSV strings. Our buffer should contain a small sequence
# of null-terminated strings that the fuzzer harness can consume in order:
# 1) Several filenames (0..3 used by the stub, we provide up to 6 to be safe)
# 2) Two CSV strings (targets CSV, architectures CSV) used by SetFnVar*Csv
# 3) Extra filenames for the SetInFiles in constructor and setter stub
# 4) Some additional strings for robustness
#
# We generate platform-friendly relative paths and diverse CSV strings to
# exercise code paths (presence/absence of commas, varying lengths, symbols).

MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 4096

def _rand_choice(rnd: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rnd.randrange(len(seq))]

def _rand_filename(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a relative path with 1-3 components, safe characters
    components = []
    depth = rnd.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(depth):
        name_len = rnd.randint(1, 12)
        # Include a mix of alnum, dash, underscore, and a dot occasionally
        chars = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_"
        base = ''.join(rnd.choice(chars) for _ in range(name_len))
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            base += '.' + _rand_choice(rnd, ["spv", "bin", "spirv", "dat", "tmp"])
        components.append(base)
    path = os.path.join(*components)
    # Occasionally prefix with ./ or a short subdir to vary
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        path = os.path.join('.', path)
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        path = os.path.join('subdir', path)
    return path

def _rand_csv(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce diverse CSV: 0-5 items, items may include dashes/underscores and digits
    count = rnd.randint(0, 5)
    items = []
    for _ in range(count):
        # Some entries mimic plausible targets/architectures; others random
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            items.append(_rand_choice(rnd, [
                "vulkan1.0", "vulkan1.1", "vulkan1.2", "vulkan1.3",
                "spirv1.0", "spirv1.3", "spirv1.5", "spirv1.6",
                "sm_50", "sm_70", "sm_90", "gfx1030", "gfx1100",
                "x86_64", "aarch64", "riscv64"
            ]))
        else:
            l = rnd.randint(1, 10)
            chars = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-_"
            s = ''.join(rnd.choice(chars) for _ in range(l))
            items.append(s)
    csv = ",".join(items)
    # Sometimes produce single item without comma, or empty string
    if rnd.random() < 0.15:
        csv = ""
    elif rnd.random() < 0.15 and items:
        csv = items[0]
    # Cap length to 512 like the stub does
    return csv[:512]

def _pack_c_strings(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # Join as null-terminated C-strings, ensure total <= MAX_TOTAL_BYTES
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b"\x00"
        if len(out) + len(b) > MAX_TOTAL_BYTES:
            break
        out += b
    # Ensure at least one null terminator exists
    if not out:
        out = bytearray(b"\x00")
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    strings: List[str] = []

    # Filenames for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME calls (constructor and setter use 0..3 each)
    # Provide up to 6 filenames to cover both loops, plus a few extras
    file_count = rnd.randint(2, 8)
    for _ in range(file_count):
        strings.append(_rand_filename(rnd))

    # Targets CSV then Architectures CSV
    strings.append(_rand_csv(rnd))
    strings.append(_rand_csv(rnd))

    # Additional filenames in case the harness requests more
    extra_files = rnd.randint(0, 4)
    for _ in range(extra_files):
        strings.append(_rand_filename(rnd))

    # A few miscellaneous short strings that could be used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR elsewhere
    misc_count = rnd.randint(1, 4)
    misc_pool = ["", "lib,exe", "a,b,c", "single", "x86_64,aarch64", "spirv1.6"]
    for _ in range(misc_count):
        strings.append(_rand_choice(rnd, misc_pool))

    return _pack_c_strings(strings)
